description:
## Substrate canon-update: team-deployment procedure for already-deployed (say-trigger) workspaces

**Type:** substrate role-file canon addition (MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md). Single-file, no code/app/other-roles. Small arc, or fold into the next substrate-canon arc.

### Motivation / empirical anchor

2026-05-21: user-tier POLYBIUS, deploying a railway_stoa recon team, used the WRONG activation mechanism — wrote root `HUMAN_paste-*.md` files (the paste-trigger mechanism) and dumped their full multi-paragraph content into chat for PRINCIPAL to copy. Both wrong for an ALREADY-DEPLOYED say-trigger workspace (where `CLAUDE.md` auto-loads the role on the bare words "polybius"/"pliny"). PRINCIPAL corrected: the instruction belongs in beadwork (a bw ticket, + optionally supporting `.md` committed to the beadwork branch); activation is just "polybius"/"pliny"; the agents self-discover via their §9 startup bw-sweep.

Root cause: MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md had the COMPONENTS (§4.5 on-disk discipline; §5 onboarding; §7.4 polling; §9 activation checklist) but never ASSEMBLED them into a single "how to deploy a team to an already-deployed workspace" procedure — and §4.5/§5 documented only the paste-trigger one-liner ("Read HUMAN_...md and execute"), not the say-trigger bw-discovery mechanism.

### Drift note

The USER-TIER deployed copy (`~/.claude/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md`) ALREADY carries both edits below (PRINCIPAL-approved 2026-05-21, applied directly to the deployed copy). This arc brings the SOURCE (`substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md`) into alignment so `install.sh` propagates §5.6 to project deployments. Until this lands, the user-tier copy is AHEAD of source — acceptable, since team-deployment is a user-tier-POLYBIUS job and the user-tier copy is the load-bearing one.

### Edit 1 — append to §4.5 (after the line "...v1 didn't make this load-bearing; v2 does.")

> **Two activation mechanisms — pick by workspace install mode (see §5.5, §5.6).** The on-disk-`.md` + `"Read HUMAN_<file>.md and execute"` one-liner above is the *paste-trigger* mechanism — for workspaces where the role is NOT auto-loaded (paste-trigger install per §5.5). For *already-deployed say-trigger* workspaces (the workspace `CLAUDE.md` auto-loads the role on the bare words "POLYBIUS"/"PLINY"), the durable artifact is a **bw ticket** (not a root `.md`) and the activation is the **bare word** `polybius`/`pliny` — the agent's §9 startup sweep discovers the instruction in bw. Full procedure: §5.6. In BOTH mechanisms the invariant holds: the substantive instruction is durable (on disk OR in bw); what the human relays is short (a one-liner or a single bare word), never a multi-paragraph chat dump. Empirical anchor: 2026-05-21 — deploying a railway team, user-tier POLYBIUS dumped full activation pastes into chat AND used the paste-trigger root-`.md` mechanism for an already-deployed say-trigger workspace; PRINCIPAL corrected — the instruction belongs in bw, activation is just "polybius"/"pliny".

### Edit 2 — insert new §5.6 (between §5.5's "...four-row table." empirical anchor and the `---` divider before "## 6. Compact-or-clear recovery")

Full §5.6 text is in the user-tier copy `~/.claude/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md` (mirror it verbatim). Heading: "### 5.6 Deploying a team to an ALREADY-DEPLOYED workspace (the 'polybius'/'pliny' say-trigger pattern)". 4-step procedure: (1) store instruction as a bw ticket [option a]; (2) optionally commit supporting `.md` to the beadwork branch via a dedicated git worktree, never `git checkout beadwork` from main per §7.5 [option b]; (3) human activates with bare "polybius"/"pliny"; (4) team self-discovers via §9 sweep, polls, handshakes, executes. Contrasts say-trigger (§5.6) vs paste-trigger (§5). Carries the 2026-05-21 empirical anchor.

### For the arc to verify (ARGUS/CATO)

- Option-b mechanism: confirm `git worktree add <tmp> beadwork` → add+commit `.md` → `git worktree remove` is sound AND does not conflict with bw's beadwork-branch file structure (bw reads its own `issues/`,`status/`,etc.; an extra `.md` should be inert — verify).
- §-numbering: §5.6 is a free slot (§5.1-§5.5 exist); no renumbering; the §4.5 cross-refs to §5.6 resolve.
- Internal consistency: paste-trigger→§5, say-trigger→§5.6; §4.5/§5.5/§5.6 cross-references coherent.
- Reference implementation = the user-tier copy; arc mirrors it verbatim (text is identical-by-construction).
- Authorship: role-file edit, no author-field changes; confirm Denson Smith unaffected.

### Out of scope

No other role files, no code, no app, no install.sh changes (the propagation is automatic on next install.sh run once source carries it).
